name: Oxalic Acid
harm_mechanisms: Binds divalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+, Fe2+, Zn2+) forming insoluble salts — reducing mineral bioavailability
Can crystallize into calcium oxalate in the kidneys, contributing to nephrolithiasis (kidney stones)
At very high doses (>2g in a single sitting) can cause acute renal failure — primarily from concentrated industrial sources, not dietary intake

neutralization.boiling: Boiling for 5–10 min in water removes 30–87% depending on the vegetable and water volume. Discard cooking water.
neutralization.soaking: Soaking in water for 8–12h removes 10–30%. Discard soak water.
neutralization.fermentation: Fermentation reduces oxalate by up to 50% in 24h (e.g., in fermented leafy greens).
neutralization.none: Raw consumption preserves full oxalate content.
